description: Rules that turn intake answers into a 4-module plan. Implement as a pure function plan(answers) -> { modules: string[], reasons: Record<string,string> } with unit tests for every rule.

rules.reason: Programmes that work start by building good moments together. Everything else is easier after that.

rules.rule: If difficulties includes 'my_stress' OR shouting == 'often': week 2 is m6_staying_calm, and m2_praise follows in week 3. Otherwise week 2 is m2_praise.
rules.reason_m6: You told us stress or shouting is hard right now, so we start with tools for you.
rules.reason_m2: Noticing what goes right is one of the most effective skills to learn early.

rules.rule: Next slot: if difficulties includes 'routines' or 'instructions' -> m3_instructions_routines. Else if it includes 'outbursts' or 'arguing' -> m4_rewards_consistency. Else -> m3_instructions_routines.
rules.reason_m3: Clear instructions and routines target the difficulty you picked.
rules.reason_m4: Rewards and consistency target the difficulty you picked.

rules.rule: Fill remaining slots up to 4 in this order, skipping modules already in the plan: m2_praise, m6_staying_calm, m4_rewards_consistency, m3_instructions_routines, m5_calm_consequences.
rules.reason: Builds on the skills you've already practised.

rules.rule: m5_calm_consequences may only appear after m3 or m4 in the plan. If the fill would place it earlier, move it later or leave it out of the 4-week plan.
rules.reason: Consequences work best once positive routines and rewards are in place.

rules.rule: After week 4, all six modules are available to revisit in any order.

weekly_adaptation.description: After each weekly check-in, suggest what to do next based on days_practised. Implement as a pure function nextStep(checkin, history) -> { recommended, options, message } with unit tests. The parent always chooses; never move them on or hold them back automatically.

options.move_on: Move on to the next module
options.repeat_short: Repeat this module with the short version
options.repeat_full: Repeat this module as it is

rules.message: Busy week? That's completely normal. A shorter version of this week's exercise might fit better. You can also repeat it as it is, or move on.
Good going. You can move on, or stay with this module for another week if it needs more practice. Both are fine.
Great practice this week. Ready for the next module?

rules.when: the same module has already been repeated twice
rules.message: You've spent a few weeks on this one. Moving on often helps, and you can come back to it any time.

effects: repeat_short: same module next week, showing short_exercise instead of exercise (full version one tap away).
repeat_full: same module next week, unchanged.
Any repeat pushes the remaining plan back by one week. The programme can run longer than 4 weeks.
Store the choice and whether the short version was used with the next check-in.
weekly_adaptation.input: days_practised is pre-filled from the parent's daily ticks for the module week; the parent can correct it in the check-in.

personal_defaults.description: Uses the two intake answers that previously had no effect.

rules.effect: Each module opens in its short version, with 'Show full version' one tap away. The parent can switch at any time.
Show the module 4 co_parent_step, and pre-select 'The other parent or carer' as practice partner in Set up your week.

already_doing.description: From the 'I already do this' button on a module.

rules.effect: This week uses the short version. Check-in and adaptation as normal.
Mark the module as completed (skipped), make the next module available now, and show the 'Coming up next week' preview. Counts as done for the consequences gate.

rules.note: Not offered for week 1 (m1_special_time) in the first plan: it is the low-effort start that later modules build on. Offered when revisiting.

test_cases_extra.expected: co_parent_step shown as last step; partner pre-selected
m3 marked done; m6 available immediately

test_cases_extra.case: already_doing on m1 in first plan
